# COLOR TRAP — MASTER MVP SPECIFICATION

> This is the master MVP blueprint for Color Trap.
> The supplied generated images are included in `references/` and are authoritative UI references.
> The implementation agent must reproduce the referenced UI rather than inventing a different visual design.

## REFERENCE ASSETS

| ID | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | `references/01-logo.png` | Official logo reference |
| 02 | `references/02-home-screen.png` | Home / intro reference |
| 03 | `references/03-instructions-screen.png` | Instructions reference |
| 04 | `references/04-gameplay-screen.png` | Gameplay reference |
| 05 | `references/05-game-over-screen.png` | Game Over reference |

![Logo reference](references/01-logo.png)

![Home reference](references/02-home-screen.png)

![Instructions reference](references/03-instructions-screen.png)

![Gameplay reference](references/04-gameplay-screen.png)

![Game Over reference](references/05-game-over-screen.png)

## NON-NEGOTIABLE REFERENCE RULES

1. The agent must inspect all five reference images before final UI implementation.
2. The agent must compare the implementation against the references after the first UI pass.
3. The agent must not design the UI from memory.
4. The agent must not substitute personal style preferences for the references.
5. The agent must not flatten the UI into generic HTML controls.
6. The agent must recreate the interactive composition with real components.
7. Dynamic values must be live data, not text baked into images.
8. Reference screenshot numbers are examples only.
9. Major placement, hierarchy, card treatment, button treatment, logo treatment, and background treatment are locked by the images.
10. The only acceptable visual deviation is one required by functionality, responsiveness, accessibility, or a technical constraint, and it must preserve the reference identity.

## 01 MASTER DIRECTIVE

**Contract:** The coding agent must treat this document as the master MVP contract.

1. Inspect the real repository before editing.
2. Inspect the matching reference image before editing this topic.
3. Use the reference image instead of personal design preference.
4. Preserve the established visual hierarchy.
5. Keep dynamic data separate from decorative artwork.
6. Use real interactive HTML or equivalent UI instead of a flattened screenshot.
7. Keep the game responsive.
8. Keep controls semantic.
9. Keep keyboard focus visible.
10. Keep touch targets usable.
11. Keep mouse and touch behavior equivalent.
12. Keep answer correctness data-driven.
13. Keep scoring independent from CSS styling.
14. Keep streak logic independent from CSS styling.
15. Keep timer logic independent from CSS styling.
16. Keep storage independent from screen layout.
17. Keep audio independent from score logic.
18. Keep platform APIs behind an adapter.
19. Keep challenge templates modular.
20. Keep the 60-second active-session contract.
21. Keep countdown outside the active timer.
22. Keep one-answer-per-challenge semantics.
23. Clear feedback before the next challenge.
24. Block input after Game Over.
25. Block input while paused.
26. Block answer input during countdown.
27. Prevent replay from duplicating resources.
28. Prevent navigation from leaving stale timers.
29. Keep decorative layers pointer-events none.
30. Do not hard-code screenshot sample values as live data.
31. Do not hard-code a correct answer position.
32. Do not use position as correctness.
33. Do not limit the game to words.
34. Include non-word visual challenges.
35. Keep questions short and unambiguous.
36. Keep distractors meaningful.
37. Keep answer options unique.
38. Keep canonical labels consistent.
39. Keep accessibility text synchronized with challenge data.
40. Keep feedback brief.
41. Keep animations lighter under reduced motion.
42. Keep sound optional.
43. Keep storage resilient.
44. Keep production builds reproducible.
45. Run the application after substantial changes.
46. Compare the running UI with the supplied reference.
47. Fix critical regressions before continuing.
48. Document intentional deviations.
49. Do not silently invent missing behavior.
1. Check the same general aspect ratio as the reference when comparing layouts.
2. Match relative size before changing implementation technology.
3. Match alignment before adding extra decorative elements.
4. Match card radius before adding component variations.
5. Match button depth before adding custom effects.
6. Match typography weight before adding new fonts.
7. Match logo scale before changing surrounding spacing.
8. Keep foreground content above decoration.
9. Keep background effects behind the interaction layer.
10. Do not let a decorative element intercept pointer events.
11. Do not crop the supplied logo.
12. Do not stretch the supplied logo.
13. Do not place new controls over the logo.
14. Do not move the primary action away from the reference focal region.
15. Do not replace a glossy button with a browser-default button.
16. Do not replace a dark panel with a white panel.
17. Do not replace neon accents with muted business colors.
18. Do not add a sidebar to gameplay.
19. Do not convert the results screen into a plain table.
20. Do not convert instructions into an unrelated carousel.
21. Keep dynamic values as actual text.
22. Keep screenshot sample numbers out of production constants.
23. Keep challenge content variable while the outer Gameplay shell stays stable.
24. Keep the question as the authority for what the player must identify.
25. Keep the target property explicit.
26. Keep the distractor property explicit.
27. Keep answer generation separate from visual rendering.
28. Keep score calculation separate from challenge generation.
29. Keep reaction timing separate from animation timing.
30. Keep pause behavior separate from render concerns.
31. Keep resource cleanup idempotent.
32. Keep edge cases explicit.
33. Keep zero states intentional.
34. Keep browser restrictions graceful.
35. Keep the game usable without an account.
36. Keep the game usable without a network gameplay service.
37. Keep the core loop fast.
38. Keep challenge transitions short.
39. Keep answer buttons in stable positions.
40. Keep keyboard mapping synchronized with visible answer order.
41. Keep touch behavior free from hover-only interactions.
42. Keep reduced-motion behavior functional.
43. Keep audio failures non-fatal.
44. Keep local storage failures non-fatal.
45. Verify desktop composition.
46. Verify narrow viewport composition.
47. Verify the result screen.
48. Verify replay.
49. Verify leaving gameplay.
50. Verify returning to Home.
51. Verify the UI again after responsive changes.

## 89 ICON STYLE

**Contract:** Icons use a consistent bold arcade treatment.

1. Inspect the real repository before editing.
2. Inspect the matching reference image before editing this topic.
3. Use the reference image instead of personal design preference.
4. Preserve the established visual hierarchy.
5. Keep dynamic data separate from decorative artwork.
6. Use real interactive HTML or equivalent UI instead of a flattened screenshot.
7. Keep the game responsive.
8. Keep controls semantic.
9. Keep keyboard focus visible.
10. Keep touch targets usable.
11. Keep mouse and touch behavior equivalent.
12. Keep answer correctness data-driven.
13. Keep scoring independent from CSS styling.
14. Keep streak logic independent from CSS styling.
15. Keep timer logic independent from CSS styling.
16. Keep storage independent from screen layout.
17. Keep audio independent from score logic.
18. Keep platform APIs behind an adapter.
19. Keep challenge templates modular.
20. Keep the 60-second active-session contract.
21. Keep countdown outside the active timer.
22. Keep one-answer-per-challenge semantics.
23. Clear feedback before the next challenge.
24. Block input after Game Over.
25. Block input while paused.
26. Block answer input during countdown.
27. Prevent replay from duplicating resources.
28. Prevent navigation from leaving stale timers.
29. Keep decorative layers pointer-events none.
30. Do not hard-code screenshot sample values as live data.
31. Do not hard-code a correct answer position.
32. Do not use position as correctness.
33. Do not limit the game to words.
34. Include non-word visual challenges.
35. Keep questions short and unambiguous.
36. Keep distractors meaningful.
37. Keep answer options unique.
38. Keep canonical labels consistent.
39. Keep accessibility text synchronized with challenge data.
40. Keep feedback brief.
41. Keep animations lighter under reduced motion.
42. Keep sound optional.
43. Keep storage resilient.
44. Keep production builds reproducible.

48. Document intentional deviations.

1. Check the same general aspect ratio as the reference when comparing layouts.
2. Match relative size before changing implementation technology.
3. Match alignment before adding extra decorative elements.
4. Match card radius before adding component variations.
5. Match button depth before adding custom effects.
6. Match typography weight before adding new fonts.
7. Match logo scale before changing surrounding spacing.
8. Keep foreground content above decoration.
9. Keep background effects behind the interaction layer.
10. Do not let a decorative element intercept pointer events.
11. Do not crop the supplied logo.
12. Do not stretch the supplied logo.
13. Do not place new controls over the logo.
14. Do not move the primary action away from the reference focal region.
15. Do not replace a glossy button with a browser-default button.
16. Do not replace a dark panel with a white panel.
17. Do not replace neon accents with muted business colors.
18. Do not add a sidebar to gameplay.
19. Do not convert the results screen into a plain table.
20. Do not convert instructions into an unrelated carousel.
21. Keep dynamic values as actual text.
22. Keep screenshot sample numbers out of production constants.
23. Keep challenge content variable while the outer Gameplay shell stays stable.
24. Keep the question as the authority for what the player must identify.

26. Keep the distractor property explicit.
27. Keep answer generation separate from visual rendering.
28. Keep score calculation separate from challenge generation.
29. Keep reaction timing separate from animation timing.
30. Keep pause behavior separate from render concerns.
31. Keep resource cleanup idempotent.
32. Keep edge cases explicit.
33. Keep zero states intentional.
34. Keep browser restrictions graceful.
35. Keep the game usable without an account.
36. Keep the game usable without a network gameplay service.
37. Keep the core loop fast.
38. Keep challenge transitions short.
39. Keep answer buttons in stable positions.
40. Keep keyboard mapping synchronized with visible answer order.

## GAMEPLAY CHALLENGE LIBRARY

The game must deliberately experiment beyond color words. Words are one tool, not the complete game.

### CLASSIC WORD TRAP
1. Show a color word in a conflicting display color.
2. Ask what color the word is written in.
3. Example: GREEN rendered in RED means RED is correct.
4. The written word is the distractor.
5. The displayed color is the target.
6. Provide four answer choices.
7. Randomize the option order.
8. Do not make the first option always correct.
9. Do not make the button position encode correctness.
10. Keep the challenge centered inside the gameplay panel.

### SHAPE TRAP
1. Show a colored geometric shape.
2. Ask which shape it is.
3. The color becomes the distractor.
4. Or ask what color the shape is.
5. The shape becomes the distractor.
6. Support circle, square, triangle, and star-like shapes.
7. Keep silhouettes clear.
8. Keep labels canonical.
9. Keep answers in the standard answer grid.
10. Do not change the outer gameplay UI for shape challenges.

### OBJECT COLOR TRAP
1. Show a visible object with multiple properties.
2. Ask for one property.
3. Use another property as the distraction.
4. Keep the requested property explicit in the question.
5. Keep correctness explicit in challenge data.

### PATTERN TRAP
1. Use readable patterns such as stripes, dots, waves, or grids.
2. Ask either for the pattern or another object property.
3. Never obscure the target color when color is the requested property.
4. Keep procedural rendering lightweight where practical.

### POSITION TRAP
1. Use multiple objects in a clearly defined scene.
2. Ask what property belongs to a specific spatial region.
3. Use top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right when practical.
4. Keep objects separated enough for instant recognition.

### SIZE TRAP
1. Use clearly different small and large objects.
2. Ask which object is largest or smallest.
3. Ask a second-order property such as the color of the largest object.
4. Keep size differences obvious.

### ICON TRAP
1. Use simple icons instead of words.
2. Examples include star, heart, lightning, target, flame, and warning.
3. Ask for icon identity, color, or another explicit property.
4. Keep the icon set visually consistent.

### MIXED TRAP
1. Combine multiple properties.
2. Example: a large red striped triangle.
3. Ask only one property at a time.
4. Use all other properties as distractors.
5. Do not create arbitrary visual noise.
6. Validate every mixed challenge for ambiguity.

## DIFFICULTY MODEL

1. The 60-second session is divided into increasing intensity phases.
2. Early seconds favor clear word and color interactions.
3. Middle seconds introduce more shapes and objects.
4. Later seconds introduce mixed properties.
5. Final seconds emphasize speed and selective attention.
6. Difficulty may change challenge template weighting.
7. Difficulty may reduce transition time.
8. Difficulty must not destroy readability.
9. Difficulty must not remove accessible labels.
10. Difficulty must not make answer targets ambiguous.
11. Difficulty configuration must live in one central module.

## SCORING MODEL

1. Correct base score is +1.
2. Fast answers can receive +3, +2, or +1 speed bonuses.
3. Recommended thresholds are under 500 ms, under 750 ms, and under 1000 ms.
4. Wrong answers do not award positive score.
5. Score is stored as numeric state.
6. Score formatting is presentation logic only.
7. Screenshot example score values must not become fixed constants.

## STREAK MODEL

1. Start each session at streak zero.
2. Correct increments streak.
3. Wrong resets streak.
4. Best streak is the highest value reached in the session.
5. Show current streak in gameplay.
6. Show max streak in results.
7. Milestones can be 3, 5, 10, 20, and 30.

1. Home visually matches the supplied Home reference.
2. Instructions visually matches the supplied Instructions reference.
3. Gameplay visually matches the supplied Gameplay reference.
4. Game Over visually matches the supplied Game Over reference.
5. Logo matches the supplied logo reference.
6. The classic word trap works.
7. Shape traps work.
8. Non-word challenges exist.
9. Mixed challenges are supported.
10. Timer is accurate.
11. Score is accurate.
12. Streak is accurate.
13. Accuracy is accurate.
14. Reaction time is accurate.
15. Replay is clean.
16. No duplicate listeners remain.
17. No duplicate timers remain.
18. Touch works.
19. Keyboard works.
20. Audio can be muted.
21. Reduced motion works.
22. Local storage failures do not crash the game.
23. The game remains usable without login.
24. The game remains usable without a gameplay network service.
25. Production build succeeds.
26. Final UI comparison has been performed.

## FINAL AGENT INSTRUCTION

Treat the five supplied reference images as the visual authority.
Do not use your own design judgment to redesign the interface.
Use your judgment only where the reference does not specify a detail.
When the reference specifies a detail, follow it.
Do not replace the visual system with a generic UI kit.
Do not reduce the project to a simple text quiz.
Experiment with different challenge visuals inside the stable gameplay shell.
Words, shapes, icons, patterns, position, size, and mixed properties are all part of the Color Trap concept.
The outer UI remains the same recognizable Color Trap arcade interface.
The content changes; the shell stays stable.
That separation is fundamental.
